He starts by taking a round utensil and adds freshly cut salad 🥒🍅🥕 that is already prepared with multiple veggies. It’s a healthy and colorful base that makes the bowl fresh and crunchy! 😍

🧀 Step 2: The Special Paneer

🍟 Step 4: The Crunch Factor
Here’s the most exciting part — he opens a packet of chips! 🥳
Whether it’s Doritos, Lays, or other chips, it’s completely your choice 😍. For this bowl, he picks Doritos, crushes the entire packet inside the mix, and blends it all together for that perfect crispy texture 🤩🔥.

🥡 Step 5: Packing the Magic
After mixing, the crunchy-cheesy salad is packed back into a chip packet! Yes, you read that right 🤯. Then he adds more sauces on top and gives it another good mix so that every bite is creamy, cheesy, and crunchy all at once 😍🤤.

🎉 The Final BYOB
And finally… your Italian BYOB is ready! 😍💥
Crispy chips, fresh salad, marinated paneer, and flavorful sauces all come together to make a snack that looks amazing and tastes even better 🤩.

snippet.title: Ballimaran Nahari Shaheen Bagh | Complete Recipe Of Ballimaran Nihari | Globalecentre Delhi Nahari
snippet.description:
Ballimaran Nahari Shaheen Bagh is the only Nahari specific brand that has multiple branches in many cities in India. Ballimaran Nahari complete recipe is what you will see in this video.
We spent whole day at Ballimaran Nahari Restaurant Shaheen Bagh and shot the Nahari making from scratch till end.
Gloablecentre Nahari videos are the ones that you all love to watch.

I shot complete recipe while making it live at BALLIMARAN NAHARI Shaheen Bagh Delhi. Ballimaran Nahari is the only Nahari specific chain in India serving in more than 15 major cities in India.

Introduction of Nahari
Nahari is a traditional dish that started during the Mughal era in Old Delhi. It was eaten by royal families for breakfast, especially in winter.

The word Nahari comes from the Arabic word Nahari, meaning “day,” because it was eaten early in the morning. The dish is made by slow-cooking meat (usually buffalo meat or mutton) overnight with spices like cloves, cardamom, and black pepper. It becomes soft, spicy, and full of flavor.

In Old Delhi, Nahari became popular among workers and common people too, giving them strength for the whole day. Even today, shops in areas like Jama Masjid and Chitli Qabar are famous for their tasty Nahari, served with naan or khameeri roti.

snippet.description:
Delhi street food under one hundred rupees hits differently, and this episode of 28 Weeks 28 States proves it again. From the lanes of Old Delhi to iconic chaat stops and metro-side classics, I spent the day tasting some of the capital’s most pocket friendly favourites.

The flavours started off bold with crispy aloo tikki, tangy chutneys, and that unmistakable Old Delhi charm. Then came the crunchy khasta kachori, followed by the chaos and nostalgia of a seventy plus year old chaat shop where papdi, dahi, and masala came together exactly the way Delhi likes it. Not everything hit the mark but the city’s character kept the energy high.

To wrap things up I chased a couple of misfires with a frozen mango stuffed with kulfi that redeemed the entire day in one bite. If you are exploring Delhi on a budget, this is the perfect trail to follow.

snippet.title: Mussoorie Tourist Places | Mussoorie Best Places to Visit | Travel Vlogs in India | EP-1
snippet.description:
Mussoorie Tourist Places | Mussoorie Best Places to Visit | Travel Vlogs in India | EP-1


Planning a Mussoorie trip from Delhi in 2026? In this detailed Mussoorie vlog, we take you through a full 2-day Mussoorie itinerary, travel cost (in Indian rupees), transport options, hotel details, local food reviews, and the best places to visit in Mussoorie for couples, families, or friends.

Our journey began with an AC sleeper bus from Delhi to Dehradun that cost us just ₹600 per person. From Dehradun, we took a cab to Mussoorie for ₹1,000. For budget travelers, we share a cheaper way to reach Mussoorie—just ₹80 by bus from Dehradun Railway Station.

We explored Mussoorie on a rented motorbike and shared detailed prices for scooty rentals, taxi rates, and parking costs so you can plan your own trip easily.

🚩 Mussoorie Day 1 Itinerary:

Our first stop was Lal Tibba in Landour, one of the highest viewpoints in Mussoorie. We reached via motorbike and paid ₹50 for scooty parking. Opposite Lal Tibba, we visited Savoy Cafe, had delicious pizza and lime soda with a scenic mountain view. The total cost was ₹700. We shared the complete restaurant review and menu so you can decide if it’s worth it.

Next, we headed to the famous Bhatta Falls, where we relaxed by the waterfall and enjoyed tea, coffee, lime soda, omelet, and Maggi. You can also try adventure activities like ziplining, giant swing, and rope cycling at Bhatta Adventure Park. We shared the entry fee (₹80), parking charges (₹30 for scooty, ₹100 for car), and ropeway ticket cost (₹150 one side, ₹250 both sides). If you use the ropeway, the park entry is free.

In the evening, we trekked to Dalai Hills, a hidden gem for sunset lovers. The trek takes 15–20 mins, and there’s no entry fee. You’ll see a stunning Buddha statue, colorful prayer flags, and panoramic sunset views.

At night, we explored Mussoorie Mall Road, tried local street food, and had dinner at Maharaja Palace, where we ordered butter chicken and naan. We shared our full food review, taste, and cost details.

🏨 Hotel Stay in Mussoorie:

We stayed just 500 meters from Mall Road at Hotel City Castle, which cost ₹1,200 per night, including breakfast. The hotel has parking space and is suitable for couples/families. We also gave a complete room tour in the video to help you decide if it’s worth booking.

🚩 Mussoorie Day 2 Itinerary:

We started the day by visiting George Everest Peak, the highest point in Mussoorie, with stunning hill views and beautiful roads for bikers and photographers.

Next, you can visit the iconic Kempty Falls, where you can swim or take a ropeway ride. We explained the ropeway cost, entry, and food options around the falls.

We then visited the Mussoorie Lake, one of the most popular tourist spots. There’s a ₹30 entry fee, and parking was free for us (two-wheeler). At Mussoorie Lake, you can enjoy paragliding (₹1,500), boating, water ball, haunted house, ziplining, and giant swing. We shared the price list of all adventure activities. We also had lunch overlooking the Doon Valley—a must-do for scenic views while eating.

In the evening, you can end your trip by visiting Gun Hill, where you can either trek or take a ropeway to the top. It offers panoramic views of the Himalayas and Mall Road.

🎒 Whether you’re planning a 2-day weekend trip to Mussoorie or a longer stay, this video covers:

As we arrived, we were guided by a panda (temple priest), who helped us through the rituals. He performed a brief pooja and handed Anubhav a pot of holy water, which he carried into the sanctum to offer to the deity. The atmosphere was intense, a sea of devotees, chants echoing in the background, and a current of energy that made the experience unforgettable.

After the darshan, we wandered into the narrow bylanes surrounding the temple, known locally as Peda Gali. Lined with sweet shops and the aroma of khoya wafting through the air, it reminded us of the iconic peda gali near Baba Baidyanath Dham. Though smaller in scale, it had the same charm, people calling out their specialties, trays of fresh peda, and that old-town warmth.

Next, we started our street food trail with a stop at Marwari Basa, a simple eatery that serves both snacks and home-style meals. We opted for a plate of rice and dal, light, nourishing, and served with that unmistakable hospitality that small-town kitchens are known for.

Our food trail continued as we headed to Ghormara, a small town known for its legendary peda. Our destination was Sukhari Mandal Peda, believed to be the oldest peda shop in the area. The owner welcomed us warmly, shared the story of the shop, and even walked us through the peda-making process- boiling the milk, stirring the khoya, and shaping the peda by hand. We tasted it fresh, soft, milky, and gently sweet. A quiet moment of indulgence.

Just outside, we spotted a bhunja cart, run by a young man who kept his space remarkably neat. The mix of roasted grains, peanuts, and spices made for a crunchy, flavorful snack. We washed it down with a hot cup of chai from a nearby stall, a comforting pause in our journey.

From there, we made our way to Trikut Parvat, a scenic spot about 15 km from Deoghar. The hill is associated with mythology and is believed to be the meeting point of the three major Hindu deities, Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. Though the ropeway was closed due to maintenance, the view of the hills and surrounding greenery offered a moment of calm after the hustle of the temples and markets.

As evening approached, we returned to Baba Baidyanath Dham for the Sandhya Aarti. Before entering, we stopped at the famous Dukhi Shah Dukan to try the Muni Samosa. Crisp on the outside, with a well-spiced potato filling, it was one of the best samosas we have had on this journey.

The episode closes with the powerful experience of Sandhya Aarti. It was a fitting end to a day filled with devotion, stories and simple food.

snippet.title: Fish, Cows, Filth & Gargbage – Ghazipur Fish Market - Trash Mountain | India New Delhi Walking Tour
snippet.description:
This walking tour of Ghazipur Fish Market in New Delhi reveals one of the filthiest fish markets in India, located just meters away from the infamous Ghazipur landfill. The market operates daily in extreme conditions, with vendors surrounded by garbage, rotting fish, flies, and unbearable stench. It's a raw glimpse into how food is traded near hazardous waste, raising serious concerns about health, hygiene, and urban neglect.
